title: Reviewing Fractions: Adding, Subtracting, and Using Visual Tools
prompt: Take careful notes on the key concepts about adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators, understanding mixed numbers, solving equations of the form t = an + be, and using counters or grids to solve fraction addition or multiplication. Use these notes to help you review and master these important math skills.

notes.heading: Key Concepts in Fraction Operations and Equations

keyTerms.term: Adding or Subtracting Fractions with Different Denominators
keyTerms.definition: Combining fractions that do not share the same bottom number by finding a common denominator first.
points: Find the least common denominator (LCD) to rewrite fractions with the same denominator.
Convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with the LCD before adding or subtracting.

keyTerms.definition: A number made up of a whole number and a proper fraction combined.
points: Mixed numbers can be converted to improper fractions to simplify calculations.
They often appear in answers when adding or subtracting fractions.

keyTerms.term: t = an + be (Finding a and b)
keyTerms.definition: An equation expressing t as a combination of multiples of n and e, where a and b are integers to be found.
points: To find a and b, use methods like the Euclidean algorithm or trial and error to solve for integer solutions.
This equation helps in solving problems involving linear combinations and divisibility.

mainPoints.heading: Adding or Subtracting Fractions with Different Denominators

sections.title: Key details
bullets: Identify the least common denominator (LCD) of the fractions involved.
Rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction with the LCD before performing addition or subtraction.

sections.title: Key details
bullets: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions to make calculations easier.
After calculation, convert improper fractions back to mixed numbers for final answers.

mainPoints.heading: Using Counters or Grids to Solve Fraction Addition or Multiplication

sections.title: Key details
bullets: Counters can represent parts of a whole to visualize fraction operations.
Grids help divide shapes into equal parts, making it easier to add or multiply fractions visually.

mainPoints.heading: Solving t = an + be: Finding a and b

sections.title: Key details
bullets: Use the Euclidean algorithm to find integers a and b that satisfy the equation.
These values help express t as a combination of multiples of n and e, useful in number theory.

Mixed numbers combine whole numbers and fractions and can be converted back and forth for easier calculations.
Visual tools like counters and grids make fraction operations clearer, while equations like t = an + be help find integer solutions in problems.

title: Math Review: Solving Shirt Price Problems with Equations, Fractions, and Systematic Trial
prompt: Get ready for a three-round brainstorm battle! You will solve problems like this: A store buys shirts for $14.99 each. The selling price is 3 times the cost. You will write an equation for the selling price of a shirt, find the selling price and markup, and use systematic trial with integers and proper fractions to explore pricing.

rounds.prompt: Round 1: Write an equation to represent the selling price of a shirt if the cost is $14.99 and the selling price is 3 times the cost. Use integers and proper fractions if it helps.
rounds.scoringRule: Earn points for writing a clear, correct equation that shows the selling price as 3 times the cost, including use of integers or proper fractions.

rounds.prompt: Round 2: Calculate the selling price and the markup on one shirt using your equation. Show your work using integers and proper fractions where needed.
rounds.scoringRule: Earn points for accurate calculations and clear explanations of the selling price and markup using integers and proper fractions.
exampleAnswers: Selling price is $44.97 and markup is $29.98

rounds.prompt: Round 3: Use systematic trial to test if 3 times the cost is a good selling price. Try multipliers like 2 1/2 or 3 1/4 and explain your reasoning about the selling price and markup.
rounds.scoringRule: Earn points for using systematic trial with integers and proper fractions, and for explaining your reasoning about pricing and markup.
exampleAnswers: Systematic trial helps find a fair selling price and good markup
